Thank you again, Madam Chair. This next report on this morning's agenda is an update on the curbside organics program.
As administration continues to prepare for the launch of the curbside organics program in 2023,
progress is being made on some key program features, including procurement of the carts, the location of cart collection,
as well as construction of the third-party processing facility.
In 2018, the administration proposed that a medium sized green cart be used for the curbside organics program.
Since that time, the administration has completed further analysis on the existing subscription program
and has collected research and feedback from other municipalities. Based on these findings,
we have determined that a larger cart would be more appropriate as the standard cut size for curbside organics program.
This larger cart is the same size as the standard cuts for the current garbage and recycling programs,
as well as the current organic subscription program.
The procurement of the carts is underway in order to be prepared for the rollout in spring of 2023.
Similarly, in 2018, we had anticipated that the collection of the organic carts could be in the front street for all households,
regardless of whether the other waste and recycling programs are currently collected.
Upon further consideration, we are intending to launch the organic program initially with the carts being collected in the same location as the existing curbside waste and recycling carts.
So, for example, if a household's waste is currently collected in the rear lane, the organic program will begin with the new green cart also be collected in the lane.
The same would be for households with front street pickup, their organics or green bin would be collected in the front street as well.
Defraining a decision specific to the organic cart collection location will allow for a comprehensive review of the collection collection location for all three streams of waste.
As the issues related to the waste carts, for example, would be similar to the new issues or to the issues for the new organic carts.
The comprehensive review would include public engagement component to ensure feedback from residents is taken into consideration as part of the overall review.
Option options would then be presented to council for consideration after implementation of the organic program.
The report also provides information on the status of construction of the third party processing facility as well as how contaminants in the organic carts will be addressed.
As our planning work continues over the next year, we plan to provide regular updates on the progress that is being made for the successful launch of the program in spring of 2023.
